stem: A client with an ostomy reports new burning under the skin barrier, and the nurse observes leakage at the edge of the wafer. What is the best action?

options.A: Change the leaking pouching system, cleanse the area, and assess the stoma and peristomal skin before applying a new well-fitted barrier
options.B: Leave the wafer in place until a fixed calendar-change day even though leakage and burning are present
options.C: Reinforce the leaking edge indefinitely without assessing the skin underneath
options.D: Remove the pouching system and leave the stoma uncovered for the rest of the day

rationale: Open RN Nursing Skills, 2nd edition, states that the pouching system must remain sealed to protect peristomal skin and that the wafer should be changed for leaking, excessive skin exposure, itching, or burning. During an appliance change, the stoma and peristomal skin are assessed.
educational_objective: Respond to leakage or burning under an ostomy barrier by changing the system and assessing/protecting peristomal skin.
source_document_title: Nursing Skills, 2nd edition — Chapter 21 Facilitation of Elimination
source_locator: Chapter 21, ostomy care, lines 397–409 and Checklist for Ostomy Appliance Change
source_claim_supported: Supports changing a wafer for leakage or itching/burning and assessing the stoma/peristomal skin during appliance change.
correction_summary: Removed the rigid routine-schedule construct and made leakage plus burning the actionable cues, which the source directly addresses.
audit_findings: A follows the source. B delays care despite explicit change indications; C fails skin assessment; D does not provide a secure collection/protection system.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11 / PDF p.15
